newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IfW sees less unemployment pressure in 1998.
newsitem.headline: German IfW sees less unemployment pressure in 1998.

text.p: Germany's unemployment levels will decline towards the end of this year, but the average number out of work in 1997 will still be 4.3 million, the Kiel economic research institute IfW said on Thursday.

The research body, which is one of Germany's six leading institutes, said ever declining numbers of newly unemployed people over the last few months pointed to a changing trend in labour markets. For 1998, the IfW forecast average unemployment at 4.1 million.
Germany's jobless rate is currently running at 11.1 percent, or 4.26 million people.
Looking at economic growth, German gross domestic product was forecast to grow at 2.6 percent in 1997 and by 3.0 percent in 1998, when domestic demand should be substantially stronger, the IfW said.
It said foreign demand and favourable monetary and wage policies would be key for economic recovery, while fiscal consolidation towards a neutral level would also boost the growth trend.

Interest rates were likely to remain steady for the rest of this year and only next year would a small tightening of monetary policy be necessary, if the economy had better established itself, the IfW said.

But it warned that any, even moderate, interest rate rise by the Bundesbank might spark conflicts with other European monetary authorities ahead of the third stage of Euroepan economic and monetary union (EMU), scheduled for January 1999.
